body:
Rookie Cade Klubnik stepped in to open the second half, leading a 10-play, 61-yard scoring drive on his very first NFL possession
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith was evaluated for a concussion after taking a hard hit at the end of the first half. He was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik temporarily before clearing concussion protocol in the second half against the Buffalo Bills.On a third-and-9 with 25 seconds remaining in the second quarter, Smith was sandwiched between defenders Terrel Bernard and TJ Parker. He remained on the turf for several moments as trainers attended to him. Check out what happened here: 
Cade Klubnik completes his first NFL driveWhen the Jets took the field in the second half, it was the rookie Klubnik under center. On the very first drive of his NFL career, he marched the Jets 61 yards downfield on 10 plays and set up a 22-yard field goal. Klubnik completed two of four passes for 39 yards and rushed twice for 19 yards. His first completion went to star wideout Garrett Wilson for 29 yards.
The fourth-round pick out of Clemson ranked top five in the FBS in completions (855), passing yards (9,426) and passing touchdowns (71) from 2023-25, and came in and beat out Brady Cook and Bailey Zappe for the backup job. 
Prior to exiting the game briefly, Smith was 9-of-16 for 113 yards and one sack taken.

title: Drake Maye, Aidan Hutchinson injured on same play: Injury updates for Patriots QB, Lions DE - CBS Sports
description: Maye and Hutchinson both went down on the final play of the first drive
body:
Maye and Hutchinson both went down on the final play of the first drive
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:00 pm ET

        Two of the game's biggest stars went down on the same play in Germany, as New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson headed to the locker room following injuries on a third-down sack on the first drive. The Patriots announced that Maye was downgraded from questionable to out with an ankle injury, and the Lions announced that Hutchinson was downgraded to out with a knee injury. Patriots backup QB Tommy DeVito took over for Maye and played the remainder of the 35-10 loss for New England. He finished 12-for-24 with 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception.  Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said he didn't have an update on Maye after the game but did say they would run more tests back in the United States to determine the severity of the injury. He called it a "lower leg" injury.When asked why Maye was ruled out despite not knowing the full extent of the injury, Vrabel said, "He couldn't function, couldn't play, couldn't run, couldn't do whatever he needed to do to play QB to protect himself to execute, or function at that level." 
Vrabel initially said there were a lot of issues he didn't believe Maye's absence affected, but then said it "may have, but I highly doubt it" when asked what his concern is without his QB1 on the offense.The head coach said the team as a whole needs to do the little things better on all three phases and work on fundamentals. He listed tackling, creating turnovers, preventing turnovers on offense, running the football, getting open, protecting the quarterback, and special teams needing to create some momentum as areas the team needs to work on, regardless of who is at QB. Bad news may be coming for the LionsAccording to reports, Hutchinson is feared to have suffered a significant knee injury, and there "does not appear hope that he returns this season." The DE immediately had an MRI and will get a second opinion, per the report.
After the game, Lions coach Dan Campbell said he had "nothing new" in terms of injury news surrounding Hutchinson, and that the team will "know more when we get back in the States.""Any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours, that doesn't make things easy. I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out ... but knowing Hutch for who he is, he doesn't stay down long," Campbell said. "... but certainly you don't want to know that a player like that is down."He emphasized how well the team adjusted and made up for a big defensive loss.On third-and-goal, Hutchinson got to the quarterback, who was limping after the play. Maye was able to walk under his own power to the sideline, but was hunched over, seemingly in pain, and eventually went to the locker room.
Here is a look at the final play of the opening drive and the last play before Maye went to the locker room:
Hutchinson appeared to injure his knee during the celebration of the sack. Here is a closer look at the celebration:
The Patriots' opening drive ended in a successful field goal attempt. The Lions immediately responded with an Amon-Ra St. Brown touchdown on their first offensive drive of the game.
Fortunately for the Patriots, they have a bye in Week 11, so they will have time to nurse these injuries before they take the field again in Week 12, when they visit the Los Angeles Chargers. The Lions will return to Detroit to host the Tampa Bay Bucanneers in Week 11.CBS Sports will continue to update this article as more news becomes available.

title: Hot seat watch: Dabo Swinney, Lincoln Riley among coaches reigniting buzz after poor Week 11 showings - CBS Sports
description: Crushing Week 11 setbacks ended playoff dreams and left fanbases frustrated, but massive buyouts complicate poten
body:
Crushing Week 11 setbacks ended playoff dreams and left fanbases frustrated, but massive buyouts complicate potential moves down the stretch
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Four Power Four programs have moved on from head coaches this season, and there could be more coming.Updating our hot seat watch coming out of Week 11, several speculative candidates negatively affected their situations after narrative-setting losses, including a couple who took their respective teams out of the College Football Playoff conversation after brief boosts of confidence. College football's coaching carousel hasn't been nearly as active this season as it was last, with sizable buyouts being a factor, along with expansive funds being earmarked for player retention and roster acquisitions in a few weeks. However, for programs whose fanbases are tuning out down the stretch, potential moves are being made behind the scenes relative to 2027 and beyond.Here are five coaches who did themselves no favors following losses on Saturday with two games left in the regular season:

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Lincoln Riley, USCSaturday's result: 27-13 loss at IndianaProjected final record: 8-4Clearly, Riley is still engaged with the Trojans and believes he can win a national championship at USC. He'll have to get to the CFP first, and that's not happening this season after another loss on the road to a ranked opponent. There were no prepared statements this time around for Riley, whose team dropped four interceptions, turned it over several times in critical situations and dropped a winnable matchup against the defending national champions.Riley's contract is private in Los Angeles, but an estimated reported price tag of around $70 million is one of the biggest in college football, and next season's allure of a 24-team playoff should buy him more time. If he gets to nine wins in 2027 — heck, even eight might do it — Riley will at least get the Trojans to their first CFP appearance and offer reason for optimism moving forward. Beating Ohio State a few weeks ago strengthened perception a bit, but losing to the Hoosiers was another black mark on his record.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dabo Swinney, ClemsonSaturday's result: 20-6 loss vs. Georgia TechProjected final record: 6-6Heavy coaching staff changes after the 2025 season haven't led to improved play from Clemson this fall, and Swinney's spiral hit all-time lows against the Yellow Jackets. Clemson is now 2-9 over its last 11 home games against Power Four competition, this coming at a program that won a school-record 40 consecutive games in Death Valley from Nov. 12, 2016 through Nov. 26, 2022. This was Clemson's first loss to a team with a losing record at kickoff since 2010, snapping a 38-game win streak, and came against a Georgia Tech squad that had fired four assistant coaches after last week's loss
Swinney's decision to bring Chad Morris back to his program to call plays has been a disastrous move. The Tigers have scored just five touchdowns in four home games this season against Power Four opponents, three of those coming in the second half of a 28-20 win over North Carolina in Week 3. The sticking point here is Swinney's cumbersome buyout. His remaining total compensation starting in 2027 is $60 million, but the Tigers would get a slight $3 million discount if the university parts ways with him this fall due to a buyout clause featuring a descending flat rate. Unlike most coaching contracts, however, Swinney's deal does not include a mitigation clause; if he takes another job, Clemson would not see its portion of the buyout reduced. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Luke Fickell, WisconsinSaturday's result: 24-21 loss at MarylandProjected final record: 7-5How does a team go from the highs of beating nationally ranked USC on Oct. 24, to being shut out by Iowa and losing on the road to dreadful Maryland over the following three-game stretch? The level of inconsistency associated with Fickell right now at Wisconsin is maddening for decision-makers, especially first-year athletic director Shawn Eichorst, who might be running out of patience waiting on things to improve for the Badgers.CBS Sports' Chris Hummer wrote this week after speaking with sources prior to Wisconsin's loss to the Terps that Fickell had "probably saved himself" getting to bowl eligibility this season, but this was another unexpected and further damning setback on the road. Fickell's now 23-25 overall with the Badgers and just 14-20 against Big Ten competition. Maryland, by the way, was under an interim coach for the third straight game following its midseason firing of Mike Locksley. Perhaps another Big Ten vacancy will surface if Wisconsin fails to deliver against Purdue and Minnesota the remainder of the month?

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Shane Beamer, South CarolinaSaturday's result: 34-6 loss at ArkansasProjected final record: 7-5Beamer bought himself more time with four consecutive wins since the Gamecocks' stunning 0-3 start to SEC play this season, but every time the program takes a step forward under his tutelage, inexcusable results like what happened in Fayetteville surface. South Carolina, as a 7.5-point road favorite and in the CFP discussion, was never competitive against the Razorbacks with quarterback LaNorris Sellers on the sideline — but was he injured? Beamer stressed after the game that his QB1 was off the SEC's final "availability report" because he was "available" to play, but the staff simply thought Cutter Woods gave the Gamecocks the best chance to win. Sellers suffered a lower-body injury in last week's win over Texas A&M and was limited throughout the week in practice, despite being listed as "probable" on Friday night before being upgraded before kickoff. Beamer's insistence on being coy with Sellers' injury status is why speculation has run rampant Sunday morning on his decision to roll with Woods, who threw three interceptions in the Gamecocks' most important game of the campaign leading into next week's tilt vs. top-ranked Georgia.The belief from boosters in early October was that South Carolina needed to beat Florida heading into its open date or that could be it for this coaching regime. The Gamecocks responded with a confidence-building win, then took out Tennessee, Oklahoma and the Aggies prior to Week 11's failure to launch on the road against one of the SEC's worst teams. Next weekend's home game against Georgia was supposed to be an opportunity to stay afloat inside the top 20 but now comes with zero stakes. A loss puts the Gamecocks at 6-5 heading to Clemson, where falling to this Tigers team puts Beamer's directly back into the job-security crosshairs.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Scott Satterfield, Cincinnati Saturday's result: 41-13 loss at Iowa StateProjected final record: 6-6Much has changed regarding Satterfield's safety with the Bearcats following his third straight setback since Cincinnati's win over then-Big 12-leading Texas Tech last month. On the verge of being ranked at 5-2 overall, the Bearcats are now .500, never found their footing at Iowa State and looked unprepared. In fact, Cincinnati's output was similar to its home bout with Utah on Halloween when Satterfield watched his defense give up 42 first-half points during a blowout loss. The rug could be pulled out from under this coaching staff if next week's game against Colorado goes south with a trip to BYU looming. Two losses mean no postseason appearance and no momentum ahead of the offseason.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kyle Whittingham, Michigan Saturday's result: 31-7 loss at OregonProjected final record: 5-7Has there ever been a more awkward fit for a first-year coach at an elite program? Whittingham has done himself no favors this season, at any point, and his comments prior to Saturday's loss at Oregon about Dan Lanning using NIL to recruit simply fell flat. He said there were no more "trophy games" after last week's 15-6 setback against Michigan State, somehow skipping over the rivalry showdown with Ohio State at the end of the month. Firing OC Jason Beck isn't going to fix what's broken in Ann Arbor, and there's a growing belief Michigan's deep-pocketed boosters are simply playing out the stretch before making a move in a couple of weeks. Does Whittingham want to deal with a rebuild with the Wolverines at his age coming off this embarrassing campaign? It's hard to see light at the end of the tunnel here with a potential mutual parting of ways being a possible outcome. His buyout percentage is also quite low at 75% (one of the lowest in the Big Ten), which means the Wolverines could move on from Whittingham after just one season in charge for the price of $24.75 million.

body:
Kenneth Walker's groin injury raises concerns for Week 10, potentially opening the door for Emmett Johnson to start
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL trade deadline did not exactly bring Fantasy blessings, outside of Minnesota. And we have four teams on a bye, including the Chicago Bears. So we need some positive injury news to keep us from scraping the bottom of the barrel for starting options in Week 10. So far, the results are best described as mixed and questionable. One guy we know we won't have is Puka Nacua, who was placed on Injured Reserve on Thursday. Nacua will be eligible to return in Week 15, the first week of the Fantasy playoffs in most leagues. His teammate, Davante Adams, could be back even sooner. For now, expect Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield to be the top receivers, though we don't want to start either. Here's the rest of the injury updates as of Friday:Jordan Addison ruled outFor those hoping to watch Addison get a chance to make plays down the field and in the intermediate areas now that Kirk Cousins is at quarterback, you're going to have to wait at least an extra week. Addison has been ruled out for Week 10 and should be removed from all lineups. Kenneth Walker misses Friday practiceHead Coach Andy Reid called it groin tightness and we would forgive Walker's Fantasy managers if they are freaking out right now. We will hope for more information as the weekend goes on but the most actionable thing I can tell you right now is make sure Emmett Johnson is rostered in every one of your leagues. If Walker has to miss the week, Walker would be a top 12 running back.George Pickens trending towards playingPickens missed last week with a hamstring injury but got some limited work in this week and has indicated he will play. Pickens has been a disappointment for Fantasy managers this season, but with four teams on a bye and several top receivers injured, Pickens is pretty much a must-start WR2. Ryan Flournoy goes back to being a touchdown-dependent flex.
Garrett Wilson and Omar Cooper Jr. should be good to goThis is fantastic news for everyone except for Adonai Mitchell managers. Wilson progressed to a non-contact jersey on Thursday and we expect him to clear the concussion protocol in plenty of time. He's a WR2 in all formats. Cooper and Mitchell are both boom-bust WR3s. We slightly prefer Cooper because he has been awesome in three of his last four games, but it is worth remembering that the last time all three Jets receivers were healthy, Mitchell had the best game. With his full complement of weapons, Geno Smith is a good streaming option.Xavier Worthy a surprise full participantWe expected Worthy to miss Week 10 but this week changed our minds. There may just be too many mouths to feed in Kansas City after the addition of Josh Downs. For now, we are projecting Rashee Rice as a WR2, Travis Kelce as a TE1, and we are waiting to see how Worthy and Downs are deployed before we start either of them. If you can only roster one, we would prefer Downs. But it may take him a couple of weeks to earn Patrick Mahomes' trust.David Montgomery returned to practice on Thursday, Woody Marks returned on FridayIf both guys play,  Woody Marks would lose all his appeal as an RB2 and Montgomery would be a touchdown-dependent flex. For now, we are still projecting Montgomery out and Marks in, which puts Marks around RB20 in a fantastic matchup against the Browns. Marks tweaked his knee at Wednesday's practice but was back on Friday and should be good to go.
Rhamondre Stevenson and A.J. Brown both questionableIn a bit of a surprise, Stevenson and Brown have gotten in limited sessions in Germany and have a questionable designation for Week 10. We have moved Brown into our rankings, and we're cautiously ranking him as an upside WR3. Demario Douglas earns a similar ranking. Douglas has seen a 20% target share in the three games Brown has played, so he should be fine in a great matchup. We still don't expect Stevenson, so Kiner is ranked as a borderline RB2. If Stevenson surprises us, we'll rank him as an RB2.George Pickens still limitedPickens missed last week with a hamstring injury after getting in multiple limited sessions and so far he is on the same path in Week 10. We aren't ranking him yet and you should have a backup plan in place. That being said, Pickens has not been ruled out yet and we are hopeful for a full practice on Friday. If Pickens is out, Ryan Flournoy is a WR3. If Pickens gets a full practice in and plays, we will rank him as a top 24 wide receiver.Zonovan Knight clears concussion protocolLike Garrett Wilson, Knight shed the non-contact jersey on Thursday. On Friday, he cleared the concussion protocol and we rank him as the best Cardinals running back this week. This is a bad matchup and Carson Beck may not have a great debut, which is why the Cardinals have an implied total of 15. In other words, neither Knight nor Wilson are ranked as starters, but if you need a flex, we prefer Knight.

It may be an awkward fit with Samuel and Keenan Allen, who the team acquired at the trade deadline. Most likely, Brock Purdy, George Kittle, and Christian McCaffrey will be the only 49ers we want to start. If Samuel is cleared, then he will be our favorite 49ers receiver, but he'll still just be an upside flex.Ladd McConkey not practicing ThursdayYou probably didn't want to trust McConkey anyway and you should plan on him being out on Monday night against the Ravens. Because it is a Monday night game, a Thursday miss isn't quite as bad, but even if McConkey were cleared, we would view him as a low-end WR3 at best. If you are desperate for a flex, Tre Harris would be our favorite Chargers wide receiver without McConkey. Of course, Harris was limited with a shoulder injury on Thursday.T.J. Hockenson misses practice on ThursdayThis one is concerning. Hockenson has a pair of ailments and could be in danger of missing Week 10, though we are still ranking him as a low-end starter. If Hockenson is out, we would be more interested in Jordan Addison as a WR3. Justin Jefferson is a must-start either way, and we would like to give Kirk Cousins a week to get comfortable before we put him in the starting lineup.
Denzel Boston listed as questionableFor what it is worth, Boston expressed optimism that he will be able to go after missing practice earlier in the week with a toe injury. We view him and KC Concepcion as both boom/bust WR3 options this week and we slightly prefer Boston if he's healthy. The Texans have not been as good as we expected defensively and have actually given up the second-most Fantasy points to opposing receivers.Travis Etienne questionableEtienne practiced every day in his first week after the team opened up the window for him to return from Injured Reserve. As of now, we are projecting Etienne to miss one more week, which would mean a committee between Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara. Both are high-end flexes, with Kamara being more valuable in full PPR leagues than he is in leagues where catches count for less. Expect Estime to lead the team in rush attempts against a bad Panthers run defense. IF Etienne returns, he will be our highest-ranked Saints running back, but no more than a high-end flex.Carnell Tate ruled outTate will miss Week 10 and a good matchup against the Jaguars. Tony Pollard is the only Titan we want to start, though Wan'Dale Robinson is a good number three receiver in full PPR leagues. Gunner Helm, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike all have sleeper appeal, but we would only start them in the deepest of leagues.

        LSU women's basketball star MiLaysia Fulwiley was arrested in Baton Rouge on Saturday after allegedly striking a police officer with a vehicle before fleeing the scene. Fulwiley is still in custody as of Sunday afternoon, according to inmate records from the East Baton Rouge Sheriff's Department. Fulwiley is facing five charges, including flight from an officer, aggravated assault and aggravated battery. Her bond has been set at $20,000. LSU told CBS Sports in a statement that they "are aware of the situation and have no further comment at this time as it's an ongoing legal matter."Fulwiley posted a since-deleted statement to what appears to be her social media account on Sunday afternoon accusing the officers of lying:
"i would NEVER in my life hit a police ! WHY would i hit a police and run knowing who i am and what i do ! PLEASE DONT BELIEVE EVERYTHING YOU SEE !," Fulwiley wrote. Fulwiley was allegedly weaving through traffic on Saturday night when an officer directing traffic ordered her to stop, according to WBRZ. After coming to a stop and handing her license to the officer, Fulwiley was asked to reverse, according to police records. She allegedly put the car in reverse, then drove forward and struck an officer with the right side of the vehicle before fleeing the scene. Later, another officer cut off Fulwiley's car, and both Fulwiley and her passenger were removed from the vehicle and placed into custody, according to police.
A spokesperson for the East Baton Rouge Sheriff's Office did not immediately return a request for comment from CBS Sports.Fulwiley transferred to LSU in 2025 after spending her first two collegiate seasons at South Carolina. She is the reigning back-to-back SEC Sixth Player of the Year and is currently projected as a top 10 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft. Through her first four games this season, Fulwiley is averaging 17.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 4.3 steals and 2.8 blocks on 54.9% shooting. LSU is off to a 4-0 start and is ranked No. 9 in the country. The Tigers will be in action next on Monday against Troy.

        Detroit Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson is feared to have suffered a "significant knee injury" while celebrating a sack on New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye on Sunday, per multiple reports. After their 35-10 international win, head coach Dan Campbell said the team will know more once they get back to the United States and Hutchinson undergoes more testing.According to the NFL Network, Hutchinson immediately had an MRI and will get a second opinion, but "there does not appear hope that he returns this season."In the replay, Hutchinson can be seen jumping in the air after the third-down sack, and his knee appears to buckle when he hits the field. He immediately fell, grabbed his leg and remained on the field for some time. Here is a look at the celebration and ensuing injury that took place during the first drive in the team's Week 10 game in Germany:
Hutchinson walked to the medical tent and eventually went to the locker room. 
Hutchinson was initially listed as questionable to return before being downgraded to out. After the game, Campbell said he had "nothing new" in terms of injury news and complimented the rest of the team for how they stepped up in the absence of such a crucial part of the defense. "Any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours, that doesn't make things easy. I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out ... but knowing Hutch for who he is, he doesn't stay down long," Campbell said. "... but certainly you don't want to know that a player like that is down."Maye also got hurt on the play, injuring his ankle. The Patriots QB did not return for the rest of the game. 
Hutchinson has been a key part of the Lions offense since joining the team as the No. 2 overall pick in 2022. He has started all 64 games he's played in for Detroit, with 48.0 sacks, 199 combined tackles, including 49 for a loss, 118 quarterback hits, 14 passes defended and five interceptions in his career heading into this week.Hutchinson missed 13 games in 2024 due to a broken left tibia he suffered in Week 6 of that season.The Lions now sit at 7-2 in a tight NFC North race. They will face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next week.

description: Gibbs is making NFL history in Germany
body:
Gibbs is making NFL history in Germany

        Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs continues to find himself in the NFL history books, and his resume just got another impressive addition on Sunday in the international game against the New England Patriots in Germany. Gibbs' first touchdown of the day marked his 61st NFL score, tying the record for most touchdowns scored through four seasons in the league. His touchdown run tied two-time Super Bowl champion and Broncos running back Terrell Davis. But Gibbs didn't stop there. His second TD surpassed Davis and put the Lions star alone in first place. The score also put the Lions up 35-10, where it would remain. Here is a look at the 28-yard record-breaking trip to the end zone in the fourth quarter:
Gibbs also became the first player in NFL history to have at least 1,000 rushing yards and 350 receiving yards in a player's first nine games of the season. After the win, Gibbs discussed what has been working for him to put up these big numbers, and he gave all the credit to his teammates, calling out the offensive line, wide receivers and tight ends.
"I couldn't do any of it without them, so I let them pave the way and whatever happens after that, happens," he said. 
His first touchdown of the game was a five-yard run in the second quarter. Here is a look at the record-tying TD:
With eight games left in the season, the chances of Gibbs extending the record are pretty high. Gibbs has nine rushing touchdowns and two in the air heading into Week 10 (eight starts), for 11 total. He is averaging 1.38 touchdowns per game. 
In the first half against the Patriots, No. 0 has an impressive 13 carries for 93 yards and tallied a total of 171 yards from scrimmage when adding in his four catches. He finished with 22 carries for 153 yards on the ground and seven receptions for 99 yards. Gibbs led the team in both rushing yards and receiving yards, coming one yard above wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, who had 98 yards and two touchdowns in the air.The Lions running back-wide receiver duo of Gibbs and Brown also made some history in their Week 10 matchup. With both making trips to the end zone this week, it marks the 24th time both players have logged TDs in the same game, passing the Buffalo Bills RB-WR duo of Andre Reed and RB Thurman Thomas, who scored in the same game 23 times. They are now third for most games scored by a running back and wide receiver duo since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.St. Brown reached the end zone for the first time since September, scoring the day's first touchdown in his mother's home country of Germany.

title: Bryce James sits in  Arizona's win vs. Auburn: What Tommy Lloyd said about son of LeBron James not playing - CBS Sports
description: The son of NBA star LeBron James logged a DNP-CD after starting Arizona's first three games
body:
The son of NBA star LeBron James logged a DNP-CD after starting Arizona's first three games
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For the first time this season, Bryce James — the son of NBA star and current 76ers forward LeBron James — wasn't in Arizona's rotation after starting the first three games of the 2026-27 season against Northern Arizona, Cal Poly and UCLA. James didn't play during the Wildcats 80-69 win over Auburn on Friday.After the game, Arizona coach Tommy Lloyd said he had a "great conversation" with Bryce and that the program will continue to find ways to "give him opportunities" to play."Bryce and I had a great conversation," Lloyd said. "I wish I would have got him in the game. It just kind of got tight there and we got the lead. ...  I went with the guys who had been out there and were able to get us that lead, and hoping they could do it again. But Bryce has really shown me a lot the last couple weeks and we'll continue to try to find ways to give him opportunities for sure."James had been a fixture in Arizona's rotation during the program's Lithuanian tour earlier this summer and in the first three games of the season before logging his first DNP-CD of the season. Lloyd opted for a three-guard starting lineup against Auburn, with JJ Mandaquit getting the start over James.

        
            
                College basketball rankings: LSU crashes Top 25 And 1 as Donovan Dent's heroics power Tigers past Gonzaga
                
                    Gary Parrish                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Arizona played just eight players during its win over Auburn, with Maksim Brnovic (six minutes), Evan Otten (eight) and Cameron Holmes (14) the only players who logged minutes off the bench. The Wildcats' rotation has been in flux to start the season due to the pending eligibility of Clemson transfer RJ Godfrey, who is currently ineligible to play."We felt like this was a really important game for our season," Lloyd said. "... But we knew coming here, I'm expecting it to be a Quad 1 win. This team's trying to establish its identity and kind of build our confidence. I I tightened the lineup today, changed the starting lineup because I wanted to put a little bit more ball handling out on the court, and that lineup has been our best lineup. James was part of Arizona's loaded 2025 recruiting class that helped the Wildcats reach the Final Four for the first time since 2001 and was expected to be a key part of the rotation during the 2026-27 campaign off the bench after redshirting during his freshman season.
Arizona has a huge matchup coming up next against No. 4 UConn on Wednesday.
